question: Should OpenClaw expose `skills-sh:owner/repo/slug` as the supported long-term public CLI contract for ClawHub-resolved unscanned catalog entries?
rationale: This is an additive but user-facing command grammar and trust model, not a repair to an established contract; the protected `maintainer` label and superseded alternate grammar show that the API direction needs an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Sponsor the colon grammar
options.body: Approve `skills-sh:` as the single documented external-reference form after isolated end-to-end proof demonstrates resolver pinning and provenance persistence.

options.title: Keep the capability internal
options.body: Do not expose a new CLI grammar until ClawHub and OpenClaw owners define a broader catalog and trust UX contract.

options.title: Choose another grammar
options.body: Ask for a narrowly revised PR if a different stable public reference syntax is preferred.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the colon grammar
recommendation.body: Approve `skills-sh:` as the single documented external-reference form after isolated end-to-end proof demonstrates resolver pinning and provenance persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: No concrete current-main owner could be established from the supplied history; the existing protected maintainer review path is the reliable routing signal.
